checks: At the origin each nonvertical through-cap has exactly half the mass, and pure-base through-caps have at least half. Opposite nonvertical through-caps bound every mark by one-half.
First profile sums unit-disk chords at offsets -3,0,3, giving values 2 at 0 and 3 and 0 at their midpoint.
Second profile sums chord lengths of radii 1,2,1. The outer contributions cancel base moments and each chord is centered in the remaining coordinate at every positive level.
The radical bounds follow from 55>49, 7>25/4 and 39>36. Their product exceeds 18 while the middle value squared is 12. Positive-power concavity would imply the failed geometric mean inequality.
Source 867dbbe22c30cda2 §§6–7 gives both exact actual profiles and the intended scope.

overlap.comparison: Uses power-concavity of sections of one ordinary convex body under orthogonal projection. It neither applies to the discrete sum over these fibers nor contains either fixed-profile obstruction.

readability: The definitions, scope, and proof order are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The two three-disk constructions disprove profile concavity, including the connected, symmetric and all-level centered case.
